A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and complete, including v1 Appendices A–E and v2 Appendix A. They describe the same PMC-based research program, despite substantial changes to the title, method and experiments. Visual inspection resolved extraction-order problems.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-3.5/GPT-4 experiments on PMC and its source datasets, plus prompting, self-consistency and distractor analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original Qwen/DeepSeek experiments, component ablations, hybrid-method evaluations and additional benchmark results, including MathTrap in Appendix A.3.3.

M1.justification: v1 proposes one-pass SLP modeling followed by satisfiability and uniqueness checks. v2 introduces VCSEARCH with anchored initialization, iterative variable-specific constraint exploration, solver-assisted LLM judging and state updates, plus integration with CoT/PAL. The double-check solver procedure is retained in Appendix A.2.3; the search framework is a substantive addition, not a renaming.

E1.justification: The four source dataset families and missing/contradictory problem types remain. v2 adds MathTrap, including geometry and algebra traps, and Robustmath symbol-interference tests. GSM-IC supplies an additional irrelevant-context benchmark, while v1's MC-V1/MC-V2 positional distractor scenarios disappear; irrelevant-context coverage itself was already present.

E2.justification: PHP disappears from the comparisons, while the SLP-style one-pass formal approach becomes the SMT comparator to VCSEARCH. Well-defined accuracy comparisons narrow from Basic, CoT, PAL and PHP alongside SLP in v1 Tables 1–2 to SMT versus VCSEARCH in v2 Table 2. CoT and PAL remain in rejection and hybrid comparisons.

E3.justification: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 are replaced by DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B and Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B/3B/7B. Eight-shot contexts become four-shot mixed contexts with explicit rejection instructions. PMC construction changes from templates/GPT-4 and human refinement to decomposition, reconstruction and two-LLM verification. R-Score is redefined, and the hybrid evaluation introduces a 1,000-problem balanced sample.

E4.justification: v1's demonstration-composition sweep, self-consistency analysis, positional distractor study and detailed comparative cases are removed. v2 tests pure versus mixed instructions across model sizes and adds component ablations isolating search and anchored initialization (Table 4). These examine substantially different explanations for robustness and false rejection.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run-level uncertainty; its self-consistency voting study concerns inference. v2 Table 3 and Appendix A.3.1 newly specify three repeated hybrid experiments and report mean ± standard deviation. This reporting addition is limited to that evaluation and does not establish increased repetitions of retained experiments.

E6.justification: The GPT-based result matrices and several appendix findings are replaced by new model, hybrid, ablation and benchmark results. For example, v2 Table 2 reports Qwen 1.5B average well-defined accuracy of 15.10% for SMT and 35.30% for VCSEARCH. These are newly reported comparisons under revised settings, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The custom R-Score functional changes substantively: v1 penalizes incorrect well-defined answers and gives zero for rejecting them; v2 removes that penalty, awards 0.5 for such rejections and normalizes by dataset size. v2 also introduces formal variable-constraint state, transition and initialization definitions in Equations 3–10. Neither version contains theorem/proof developments.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from SLP and two novel evaluation metrics to VCSEARCH's dynamic search and improved formal modeling. v2 adds claims about overcoming one-pass formalization difficulties, improving rejection accuracy by at least 12% across LLMs and supporting smaller models. The general reasoning-versus-rejection trade-off claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 attributes improvements to iterative decomposition and anchored initialization, including an explanation of excessive rejection without initialization. Limitations shift from v1's elementary-task scope and backbone dependence to search overhead and false rejection of valid problems unsuitable for formal modeling. Appendix A.3.3 also qualifies MathTrap performance through conservative rejection of problems the method cannot confidently solve.

D1.justification: v1 provides solver pseudocode, full method/baseline prompt sets and temperature=0. v2 supplies refinement and verification prompts, solver return categories, final PMC subset counts and hybrid sampling details, but omits the actual four-shot initialization/baseline contexts and decoding temperature. The future code/benchmark release promise also disappears; this does not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around neuro-symbolic methods, adding discussion of Logic-LM, SatLM, LOT and their formalization difficulties. It compares PMC's scope with MathTrap and adds small-model reasoning literature. v1's broad few-shot survey and first-use claim for SMT in robust mathematical reasoning give way to novelty centered on dynamic search.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Problem analysis moves before the method, experiments are organized around three research questions, and solver background moves into the appendix. Appendices A–E are reorganized into Appendix A subsections, while limitations move before the references.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. The benchmark illustration is redrawn, the SLP pipeline is replaced by a variable-constraint search diagram, and prior analysis plots give way to instruction/model-size displays. Tables are substantially reorganized into separate rejection, accuracy, hybrid and ablation comparisons, with new dataset-count and MathTrap tables.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful component ablations, broader test scenarios, repeated hybrid evaluations and more concrete limitations. However, it removes full prompt contexts and solver pseudocode, replaces documented human review of PMC with two-LLM verification, and narrows well-defined baseline comparisons. Reporting inconsistencies also limit confidence: Table 1 gives Qwen 7B PAL a Missing-type average of 79.97 although all four contributing values exceed 82. These material gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
